paper.title_en: Jordan-frame reconstruction of Einstein-Rosen-type geometries in generalized Brans-Dicke theory
paper.abstract_en: We investigate vacuum generalized Brans-Dicke theory with scalar-dependent coupling <math display="inline"><mi>ω</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> in an Einstein-Rosen-type metric. Let <math display="inline"><mi>W</mi></math> be the area density of the two-dimensional Killing orbits, <math display="inline"><mi>ϕ</mi></math> the Brans-Dicke scalar, and <math display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>W</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></math> their composite area density. On regions where the gradient of <math display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> is non-null, we impose <math display="inline"><mi>W</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> and local invertibility of <math display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>. The scalar equation admits the exact first integral <math display="inline"><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>ω</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>κ</mi></math>, where <math display="inline"><mi>κ</mi></math> is a signed integration constant, giving direct and inverse reconstruction of the coupling. For <math display="inline"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>/</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>*</mo></msub><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>a</mi></msup><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></mrow></msup></math> one obtains <math display="inline"><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>ω</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. The choices <math display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>ρ</mi></math> and <math display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>t</mi></math> define the spacelike- and timelike-gradient branches, each yielding a closed exact solution family. Their mode functions obey the cylindrical Einstein-Rosen and Euler-Poisson-Darboux equations, respectively. In the Einstein frame the normalized scalar is <math display="inline"><mi>σ</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></msqrt><mi>ln</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>/</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>, while <math display="inline"><mi>q</mi></math> cancels from the metric. In the spacelike branch the scalar contributes to the radial C-energy profile separately from the tensor flux, and the reconstructed smooth-mode class has no curvature-regular axis. In the static subclass, <math display="inline"><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> reproduces the circular-speed law of a singular isothermal dark-matter halo, while <math display="inline"><mi>q</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></math> gives a local correspondence with the rising inner NFW rotation curve. The homogeneous timelike subclass is locally Bianchi I, reduces in the Einstein frame to an exact scalar-Kasner geometry, and has a Jordan-frame effective Planck mass that evolves monotonically with Jordan-frame comoving proper time on each connected time interval on which the reconstructed scalar profile is locally invertible.
